findings.description: App::FeaturePython scratch instances have no Joint proxy attached -- Distance/Distance2/Angle permanently read __MISSING__
findings.disposition_reason: SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-25T06:25:06Z entry's disposition for this finding. The prior fix (bare doc.addObject() + JointObject.Joint() wrapped in defensive try/except) was verified live against a spawned FreeCADCmd instance and found to be a SILENT NO-OP: JointObject.Joint() on a bare document object raises "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'Type'" (it needs an owning Assembly whose Type attribute JointObject.py reads) -- the except was swallowing this every time, so the fix looked complete in code review but produced zero actual improvement. Corrected to mirror assembly_ops.py's real setup: create/reuse a scratch Assembly::AssemblyObject with Type='Assembly', get its JointGroup via UtilsAssembly.getJointGroup(), create the App::FeaturePython there, then attach the Joint proxy. Verified live end-to-end via the actual build_remote_scan_code() pipeline: all 12 App::FeaturePython properties (Angle, AngleMax, AngleMin, Distance, Distance2, EnableAngleMax, EnableAngleMin, EnableLengthMax, EnableLengthMin, Label, LengthMax, LengthMin) now resolve to real property-type-id strings, zero __MISSING__. This is the clearest instance in this whole session of why 'looks complete + passes review' isn't the same as 'verified' -- the bug was invisible without live FreeCAD.

findings.description: The varset_operations tool schema typed set_property's value as string/number/boolean only, but add_property's type field openly allows list/link types (App::PropertyStringList, App::PropertyLinkList, ...) whose natural value shape is a JSON array -- no schema-valid way existed to set such a property.

if varset.TypeId != 'App::VarSet': return f"Object {varset_name} is not a VarSet" was hand-copied verbatim in all 8 operation methods; BaseHandler.resolve_object had no type_id parameter to fold the check into the existing resolve call.

VarSetOpsHandler.bind_property was a near-verbatim copy of SpreadsheetOpsHandler.bind_property. The predicted failure mode already manifested: the concurrent full-review pass hardened varset's copy (PropertiesList-existence check, post-recompute _check_feature_state guard) without touching spreadsheet's copy, leaving the same silent-success-on-typo bug live in spreadsheet_ops.py.

remove_property called the public list_references() (a JSON string) and json.loads()'d it back into a dict, and list_references() independently re-resolved the same already-resolved VarSet -- a redundant object lookup plus a stringify/parse round trip for what both callers use as an in-process query.

_PROP_DYNAMIC_BIT = 21 is a hardcoded, unversioned FreeCAD-internal status bit with no name in FreeCAD's status-name table, gating remove_property's locked/built-in safety check with no runtime validation that the bit still means what this handler assumes.
findings.disposition_reason: converted to a fail-loud one-time runtime check (_verify_prop_dynamic_bit) rather than eliminating the hardcoded bit itself, since FreeCAD exposes no alternative public API for this -- a future renumbering now refuses with a clear error instead of silently misclassifying properties
